title: University at Buffalo: One Further Hike Late This Year May Be Appropriate, No Urgency
summary: Williams turns the market-borrowed framing of his London remarks five days earlier into his own forecast-conditioned path: if the economy evolves broadly as he projects, 'one further upward adjustment of the federal funds target range may be appropriate late this year.' The balance of risks has shifted, with employment risk receding as demand strengthens and price-stability risk rising; he now expects 'somewhat larger and longer-lasting effects from energy prices' and flags the AI-related demand shock, where demand is outrunning supply and higher input costs are starting to reach other prices, as increasingly salient. Getting inflation back to 2 percent is 'job No. 1.' The hawkish case is tempered by reassurance on the underlying picture: tariffs are no longer adding to goods inflation, housing services are decelerating, the labor market is not adding to inflation, expectations remain anchored, and he sees no evidence of spillover into broader and more persistent inflation, with inflation projected just above 2 percent next year. After the September hike he stresses 'there is no need for urgency' and time to gather data, so the extra hike is gradual and data-conditioned rather than pressing.

key_quotes.quote: If the economy evolves in a manner broadly consistent with my forecast, one further upward adjustment of the federal funds target range may be appropriate late this year to support a timelier return of inflation to target.
key_quotes.context: His own conditional policy path, stated in the conclusion.

key_quotes.quote: With the policy action we took at our September meeting, there is no need for urgency, and we have time to gather more information.
key_quotes.context: Pace qualifier immediately before the forecast-conditioned hike.

key_quotes.quote: In particular, the inflationary impact of the AI-related demand shock is increasingly salient, and I now expect somewhat larger and longer-lasting effects from energy prices on inflation.
key_quotes.context: Why the balance of risks has shifted toward price stability.

key_quotes.quote: Importantly, although we are seeing the effects of tariffs, the conflicts, and the AI surge on prices of certain categories of goods, we have not seen evidence of these spilling over into broader and more persistent inflation.
key_quotes.context: The main dovish offset in his inflation assessment.
